claims.text: The target and untreated baseline material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Electrospark deposition can produce an HfNbTaTiZr coating.
Applying an electrospark-deposited coating to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr could improve its oxygen resistance.
The relevant structural mediator is the coating composition and microstructure.
Electrospark deposition can form a compact, homogeneous coating approximately 20 micrometers thick.
Electrospark deposition produces minor surface cracks associated with rapid cooling, while such cracks may be absent through the coating cross-section.
The coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the coating would reduce oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Coated specimens will exhibit lower mass gain per unit area than uncoated specimens.
Coated specimens will develop a thinner oxide layer than uncoated specimens.
The proposed protection is applicable in air over 800–1000 degrees Celsius for five-hour exposures without external loading.
The specified coating thickness is 20 micrometers with a tolerance of plus or minus 5 micrometers.
The exact oxidation-protection mechanism and the effect of minor coating cracks on high-temperature oxidation are not fully understood.

A controlled test will expose coated and uncoated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr specimens to air at 800 degrees Celsius for five hours and measure mass gain and oxide thickness using post-exposure analysis including SEM.
Improvement is defined as a coated-specimen mass gain below 5 mg/cm² or an oxide thickness below 10 micrometers, relative to the uncoated control.
